dedupe_keys.name: geospatial dataset of gnss anomalies from aircraft and political violence events 2023 0 5 degree grid

description: This dataset, published on Zenodo by authors at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, Mevocopter Aerospace and Loxodrome Labs, joins GNSS anomalies seen in aircraft position reports with political violence events from ACLED on a global grid of 0.5 by 0.5 degree cells for 2023. For every cell and day with air traffic it counts flights, GNSS position jumps (possible spoofing) and gaps in tracks (possible jamming), their densities per flight, and the ACLED events with their disorder type, event type and subtype. Three CSV files give all 6,777,228 cell-days with traffic, the 718,237 cell-days with anomalies, and 25,770 monthly cell summaries. Coverage: global where aircraft fly, all of 2023. Format and access: CSV files (about 0.9 GB with a PDF readme) free of charge under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: anomalies are inferred from ADS-B tracks, not measured interference; gaps can have other causes; ACLED terms apply to the conflict fields. Simulation uses: mapping where GNSS-dependent systems such as aviation, shipping, telecom timing and power grids face interference linked to conflict, and exposure layers for resilience studies. Related records: GPSJam gives daily interference maps from similar aircraft data; the Laura Bassi and Jammertest datasets give receiver-level recordings.
